subject: MAP proposal: phased evaluation -> commit roadmap and TPM milestones
messages:
From: Lisa Hammond <lisa.hammond@finapps.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: MAP/Eval: timeline & TPM targets

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost numbers looked promising for our use case. We have an internal kickoff on Monday and I want to align on a realistic MAP and evaluation window before we involve Procurement. A few asks from our side: 

- We need a 3-month evaluation with success criteria (accuracy on intent routing, 95th pct latency under 300ms).
- If we hit those criteria, we want a committed plan across months 4–12 with a ramp (monthly TPM targets).
- We have a fixed budget for Q1 and would prefer a staggered ramp rather than an immediate commit to the full TPM.

Can Redwood propose a phased commit schedule with pricing and discount breakpoints tied to MAP milestones? Also please share any standard contract cadence (SOW -> MSS -> PO) and typical vendor redline timeline so I can prep Procurement.

Attaching our high-level evaluation checklist.

Thanks,
Lisa Hammond
VP Product, FinApps Inc
attachments: finapps_eval_criteria.xlsx
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Hammond <lisa.hammond@finapps.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Dec 2025 10:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP/Eval: timeline & TPM targets

Lisa — great to hear from you and thanks for sharing the checklist. We can absolutely structure a MAP that begins with a 3-month evaluation and transitions to a phased commit. Below is a practical proposal to align expectations and make Procurement's review straightforward.

Proposed MAP (high level)
- Phase 0 (Week 0): Kickoff + baseline metrics defined (owner: FinApps)
- Phase 1 (Months 0-3, Evaluation): 50k TPM/month trial allocation, access to Redwood hosted sandbox, success criteria: 92% top-intent accuracy OR latency SLO met; weekly syncs.
- Phase 2 (Months 4-6, Early Ramp): Commit to 150k TPM/month (month 4 start), 10% volume discount applied across months 4-6 if success criteria met by month 3.
- Phase 3 (Months 7-12, Full Ramp): Commit to 400k TPM/month by month 9 with staged increases (200k in month 7, 300k in month 8, 400k month 9+). Additional 15% discount on unit rates after full ramp sustained for 2 months.

Pricing/Discounts (illustrative)
- Evaluation: usage-based, no minimum, capped to 50k TPM/month for trial
- Early Ramp discount: 10% off published per-token rate if MAP success criteria met and contract signed within 14 days of Phase 1 close
- Full Ramp discount: incremental 15% (stackable with early ramp) once sustained commit thresholds are met

Operational notes
- We will provide a draft MAP doc (attached: redwood_MAP_draft_v1.pdf) you can share with Procurement.
- Legal: standard MSS with a 45-day redline turnaround (we'll loop Legal early).
- Technical: Aditya will scope any data access, SSO, and KV cache pre-warm steps once you confirm target models and sequence length distribution.

If the staggered numbers above look feasible, I can update the MAP to include specific acceptance tests and draft a SOW with the proposed discount schedule for Procurement. Shall I loop Legal now, or wait for your confirmation on the ramp numbers?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_MAP_draft_v1.pdf
From: Krishna Patel <krishna.patel@finapps.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Lisa Hammond <lisa.hammond@finapps.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Dec 2025 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP/Eval: timeline & TPM targets

Thanks Grace — helpful. A couple of clarifications from my side (Procurement + Finance):

- Our Q1 budget constrains our committed spend; we can only commit to a blended monthly spend that approximates 200k TPM average across months 4–6 (not 150k floor). Can Redwood do a three-month averaged commit (e.g., commit 600k across months 4–6) and allow month-to-month ramp within that window?
- On discounts: Procurement prefers an upfront committed volume rebate rather than stacked month-by-month discounts. Would Redwood be open to a single tiered rebate based on total committed TPM in months 4–12 (for example: 5% for 1–3M TPM, 12% for 3–6M TPM, 18% for 6M+ TPM)?
- Timeline: Our target is contract execution within 30 days after the 3-month evaluation, but we might need a short extension if legal redlines take longer.

We also want to add a success criterion: cost-per-conversation must remain within 20% of the baseline in your sandbox.

Krishna
Director, Procurement — FinApps
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Krishna Patel <krishna.patel@finapps.com>, Lisa Hammond <lisa.hammond@finapps.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP/Eval: timeline & TPM targets

Krishna / Lisa — thanks for the clear counterproposal. We can accommodate the averaged commit approach and the single-tiered rebate structure; below are concrete alternatives that map to your ask. I'm looping in Monica (Legal) to flag contract cadence and any potential MSS exceptions. Aditya will confirm SSO/metrics instrumentation for the cost-per-conversation check.

Alternative commercial options
Option A (Averaged Commit + Tiered Rebate) — preferred for budget predictability
- Commit: 600k TPM total across months 4–6 (averaged 200k TPM/month)
- Rebate: 5% for 1–3M TPM, 12% for 3–6M TPM, 18% for 6M+ TPM (applies to aggregate committed TPM for months 4–12)
- MAP milestone: contract signature within 30 days after evaluation close to lock rebate tier; if Legal needs more time, we can provide a 14-day courtesy window to finalize redlines without losing current tiering

Option B (Stagger + Performance Accelerant) — preferred if you expect faster growth
- Commit ramp: 150k (month 4), 250k (month 5), 400k (month 6+); rebate milestones tied to sustained throughput rather than aggregate commit

Operational commitments
- Acceptance tests: Aditya will propose two reproducible tests for intent accuracy and cost-per-conversation; passing both locks Phase 2 discounts.
- Instrumentation: We will provide a shared dashboard (read-only) for FinApps and weekly token consumption reports during evaluation.
- Legal: Monica — can you confirm MSS redline SLA and any standard procurement concessions (e.g., limited indemnity addendum)?

Next steps
1) Lisa/FinApps to confirm preferred option (A or B) and whether Procurement accepts aggregated rebate tiers.
2) Upon confirm, Redwood will revise MAP PDF to include exact acceptance test definitions and draft SOW for Procurement review.
3) If accepted, draft MSS sent to FinApps within 3 business days for redline.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you prefer to run through the tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
